# China turnover-surge early-rotation signal — Phase 0 (26y Shenwan)

*Generated by `scripts/china_turnover_surge_phase0.py`.  Panel: 32 Shenwan L1 sectors, 1999-12-30 → 2026-07-02, 299 monthly rebalance dates.*

**Signal:** z-score of log(20d-mean turnover 成交额) vs trailing 250d distribution, then cross-sectionally demeaned across sectors each date.  **Target:** sector forward return MINUS EW-of-all-sectors over the same horizon (relative performance, not absolute).  **Lagged variant (d-21):** signal is shifted forward 21 calendar business days — if volume truly LEADS price, the lag should preserve the IC; if the signal is merely COINCIDENT, the lag should kill it.

## Verdict

**DEAD** — Across 299 monthly rebalances (1999-2026) and 31 Shenwan L1 sectors, the cross-sectionally-demeaned turnover-surge signal has a near-zero and slightly NEGATIVE mean IC at every horizon tested: contemporaneous HAC-t −1.02 (20d) / −1.28 (60d), lagged d-21 HAC-t −1.12 / −1.09, all with raw p > 0.20. BH FDR rejects zero of the twelve cells at 10%. The event study confirms the direction: top-decile surge months return −0.21% LESS than other months over the next 20 days (t = −1.47, p = 0.14). The one hint of signal in the 2021+ era (contemporaneous HAC-t −2.09, p = 0.037) points the WRONG WAY — surging-volume sectors underperformed by 7.5% on average over the next 20 days, consistent with hot-money crowding and mean-reversion rather than early rotation. The lagged variant in 2021+ (HAC-t −1.46, p = 0.14) weakens relative to the contemporaneous, which would also falsify a leading interpretation. The hypothesis that retail volume LEADS sectoral price leadership in A-shares is **not supported** by 26 years of Shenwan data. If anything, volume surges are a mild contrarian SELL signal in the post-2021 era — the opposite of early-rotation leading.
